text:
marta: quick post-DR note: during the planned swap one EU tenant ended up stuck in "degraded" for ~12m. traffic had been routed to standby but writes were rejected due to residency-consent mismatch.

raj: can you paste the proxy/controller headers?

marta: proxy emitted:
```
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.internal
X-Region-Lease: eu-west-1;owner=proxy-7;lease-ts=1713607720
X-Consent-Flag: tenant=acct-992;consent=europe_only
X-Trace: ab12-...
```
controller KV entry looked like:
```
/leases/acct-992 -> owner: controller-3; region: eu-central-1; event_id: evt-3a9f
```
but proxies were still honoring eu-west and there was no `event_id` on the proxy side to join.

emily: sounds like two problems: 1) controller wrote a different region (eu-central) while proxies thought eu-west; 2) lack of event correlation and lack of consent-override visibility.

tom: why would controller pick eu-central? replication lag? placement policy?

marta: controller log: `placement: prefer-primary-if-consent_missing` and a downstream placement refresh failed because the consent service returned 504. Controller fell back to default region table which returned eu-central.

raj: so the placement fallback path is silently violating tenant residency. that's bad. we need explicit fail-open vs fail-closed semantics for consent queries.

emily: +1. proposal: change controller behavior to "fail-closed" for tenants with any residency flag. If consent service times out, controller should mark the event with reason `consent-unavailable` and block automatic swap. Operators should be able to force-swap with a documented override.

marta: ops visibility part: add `lease_event_id` to X-Region-Lease header and emit a short `lease_event{tenant,region,event_id,reason}` JSON into operator timeline. Example header: `X-Region-Lease: eu-west-1;owner=proxy-7;lease-ts=1713607720;lease_event_id=evt-3a9f`

raj: and add `X-Consent-Source: cache|service` so we know where the consent decision came from.

tom: metrics: `consent_query_success`, `consent_query_latency`, `lease_event_ack_latency`, and `lease_swap_conflict_count`. Add alert when `lease_swap_conflict_count > 0` for 1m.

emily: runbook: on `consent-unavailable` create a human-in-loop flow: ops receives alert with tenant+event_id, can inspect consent service, then either approve force-swap or rollback. Provide a single-click action in UI that attaches operator id to the forced event.

marta: compatibility: proxies can start emitting `lease_event_id` immediately as an optional param. Controller will backfill event ids on KV writes once we deploy. Timeline join should be tolerant if event_id missing.

infra-bot: [note] scheduled follow-up: small RFC + canary next wed 09:00 PT. owners: marta(controller), raj(placement), emily(ops-runbooks), tom(metrics).

raj: QA: what about active-active tenants who accept multi-region writes? consent flag will be `multi` and controller logic stays the same. Only `europe_only` / `region-restricted` get fail-closed semantics.

emily: good. Add end-to-end test in DR harness: inject consent-service 504 and assert controller doesn't autoroute away from primary.

marta: I'll draft RFC today and include header wire spec, controller event model, prometheus metric names, and runbook actions. Link when ready.

tom: tiny nit: standardize header name to `X-Lease-Event-Id` (kebab) to be consistent with other headers.

marta: fine with that. using `X-Lease-Event-Id` and `X-Consent-Source`.

emily: :thumbsup:

raj: thanks all. timeline reduction target: surface the reason in operator UI in <30s and reduce tenant-stalled incidents to 0/DR-run.

infra-bot: [reminder] RFC draft due EOD.
